A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DyMO research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching retained content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation comparisons, component ablations, timing results, and human evaluations in Tables 1–4, Figure 6, and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds a Llama-based ablation, GenEval evaluation, and scheduling-boundary sensitivity analysis.

M1.justification: The semantic graph, attention-alignment loss, preference guidance, adaptive weighting, Polyak update, and recurrent strategy remain unchanged. The explicit reward formula and multi-token handling clarify previously unspecified details; they do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds GenEval evaluation covering single objects, two objects, counting, colors, position, and color attribution (Section 8.4, Table 5). This adds targeted compositional coverage within the existing text-to-image task; Pick-a-Pic, HPSv2, and PartiPrompts are retained.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged. The new GenEval table extends the same SD V1.5 comparison roster from Table 1; the Llama experiment is an internal DyMO ablation.

E3.justification: New experiments substitute a Llama-based 70B model for GPT-4, vary the two scheduling boundaries through grid search, and introduce GenEval category scores. Existing sample counts and human-study designs remain unchanged. The newly stated 50 denoising steps disclose a setting without establishing a protocol revision.

E4.justification: v3 adds two focused checks: dependence on the LLM used for semantic extraction (Table 3) and sensitivity to scheduling boundaries t1 and t2 (Section 8.6, Figure 9). The existing component, recurrence, reward-level, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for the comparisons. The new results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds a substantial object-level result suite in Table 5: DyMO scores 0.57 overall versus FreeDom's 0.52, but trails FreeDom on counting (0.47 versus 0.64) and SPO on position (0.07 versus 0.11). It also adds Llama results and scheduling-response surfaces. Existing comparison scores and prior ablation results are unchanged; these are additional findings, not improved same-setting results.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the graph definitions: Equation 7 replaces a sum-of-pairs expression with an explicit positive-edge set, and the node definition distinguishes attribute elements from attribute sets. These are limited formal-definition corrections; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free alignment, semantic guidance, dynamic scheduling, plug-and-play applicability, and superior performance. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the Llama experiment as evidence of LLM-agnostic prompt analysis and the grid search as evidence of scheduling insensitivity. It adds a rationale for choosing boundaries (800, 500) and links GenEval performance to multi-object semantic alignment. The ethical discussion and future acceleration direction remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies 50 inference steps, identifies the 70B Llama configuration, explains attribute correspondence for multi-token objects, and writes out the CLIP-style preference-score formula. Hardware, existing dataset sample counts, and the project-page link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the GenEval paper by Ghosh, Hajishirzi, and Schmidt to support the new evaluation. The remaining cited works and the positioning relative to training-based alignment and training-free guidance are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the methodology overview and graph explanations, standardizes references to semantic alignment loss, and adds appendix subsections for the new evaluations. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds GenEval Table 5, scheduling Figure 9, and a Llama row in Table 3. Existing figures and tables are resized or relocated, including grouping Figures 3 and 4 together. Supplementary galleries, prompt tables, and survey screenshots are retained with updated numbering.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens the paper through object-level evaluation, checks of LLM dependence and scheduling sensitivity, and clearer technical definitions. These additions improve support for the unchanged method, although GenEval reveals mixed category rankings and uncertainty reporting remains absent. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement rather than a major advance.
